items.question: What substance destroys wrinkles and gray hair when properly recognized?
premises: A specific radiance was described previously
That radiance should be known as nectar
This nectar destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: The previously described radiance is to be recognized as nectar that destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: One should know that to be nectar, which destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What bodily condition results from the nectar that removes aging signs?
premises: The nectar removes wrinkles and gray hair
The practitioner becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair
The practitioner becomes devoid of all diseases
items.inference: Through this nectar one becomes free from wrinkles, gray hair, and all diseases.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and devoid of all diseases.

items.question: Where should the tongue be applied to bring about the destruction of disease?
premises: The tongue is the instrument of practice
The root of the palate is the specified location
The purpose is the destruction of disease
items.inference: One should apply the tongue at the root of the palate for the destruction of disease.
items.plain_english: One should indeed apply the tongue at the root of the palate for the destruction of disease.

items.question: How should the tongue be positioned within the mouth during this practice?
premises: The tongue must be contracted
This contraction should be done always
The tongue should be joined within one's own mouth
items.inference: One should always contract the tongue and keep it joined within one's own mouth.
items.plain_english: One should always contract the tongue, keeping it joined within one's own mouth.

items.question: What mental state is attained by placing the mind in the heart?
premises: The mind should be placed in the heart
This placement is maintained over time
The practitioner reaches the state of unmanatā
items.inference: By placing the mind in the heart, one attains the state of unmanatā.
items.plain_english: Having placed the mind in the heart, one remains until the state of unmanatā is attained.

items.question: What well-guarded secret concerning time has now been revealed to the goddess?
premises: The deception of time is a secret teaching
This teaching was previously well guarded
It has now been made manifest
items.inference: The well-guarded secret of deceiving time has been revealed.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the well-guarded deception of time has now been made manifest.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section concerning the emergence from the moon island?
premises: The text refers to emergence from the moon island
A chapter number is specified
This marks the sixth chapter
items.inference: This is the sixth chapter in the section on emergence from the moon island.
uncertainties: Exact meaning of candra-dvīpa-vinirgate is context-dependent
items.plain_english: Thus ends the sixth chapter in the section on the emergence from the moon island.

items.question: What teaching does the goddess request after declaring the lord her sole refuge?
premises: The goddess addresses the lord as her sole refuge
She requests an explanation
The requested topic is the three principles
items.inference: Having taken the lord as her sole refuge, the goddess asks him to explain the three principles.
items.plain_english: O Lord, tell me about the three principles; I have come to you alone as my refuge.

items.question: How should one contemplate what is located in the goddess's wheel?
premises: Something in the goddess's wheel is to be contemplated
The contemplation is compared to the moon
The comparison refers to the moon on the first lunar day
items.inference: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel as one contemplates the moon on the first lunar day.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel, just as the moon is seen on the first lunar day.

items.question: Where is the subtle flame said to be absorbed in this contemplative practice?
premises: A flame is present in the contemplation
This flame is absorbed
The place of absorption is the bone wheel
items.inference: The flame is absorbed there in the bone wheel.
uncertainties: asthi-cakre may refer to a specific subtle center
items.plain_english: And there indeed, O beautiful-faced one, the flame is absorbed in the wheel of bone.

items.question: What qualities characterize the form that destroys wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: A form is to be contemplated
This form is fluid and black
This form destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: The contemplated form is fluid, black, and destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: It is a fluid, black form, and it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What kind of yogic application should be practiced in the region of the support?
premises: The practice is located in the ādhāra region
Yoga should be applied there
The yoga is characterized as cool
items.inference: One should apply the cooling yoga in the region of the ādhāra.
uncertainties: skandha here may mean region or base rather than shoulder
items.plain_english: In the region of the ādhāra, one should practice the cooling yoga.

items.question: How should the practitioner regard the sun and the moon in this yogic visualization?
premises: The sun is to be seen as an enemy
The moon is to be seen as a friend
This contrast guides the visualization
items.inference: One should regard the sun as an enemy and the moon as a friend.
items.plain_english: One should see the sun as an enemy and the moon indeed as a friend.

items.question: What kind of physical location is suitable for undertaking this yogic practice?
premises: The practice should be done in an earthen house
The place should be solitary
The place should be free from gnats and mosquitoes
items.inference: A suitable place is a solitary earthen house free from gnats and mosquitoes.
items.plain_english: In a solitary earthen house, in a place free from gnats and mosquitoes.

items.question: What additional qualities make a place auspicious for this yogic discipline?
premises: The place should be secluded and deserted
The place should be divine in character
The place should be adorned with abundant flowers
items.inference: An auspicious place is secluded, deserted, divine, and adorned with abundant flowers.
items.plain_english: In a secluded, deserted, divine place adorned with an abundance of flowers.

items.question: What level of attainment is realized after six months of this practice?
premises: The practice yields results over time
After six months perfection is known
This perfection is equal to the state of a yoginī
items.inference: After six months, one attains a perfection equal to the state of a yoginī.
items.plain_english: After six months, perfection is attained, equal to the state of a yoginī.

items.question: From which knot are the three principles said to be situated in this teaching?
premises: The brahma knot is mentioned as a location
Three are indicated
The goddess is addressed directly
items.inference: The three are situated from the brahma knot onward.
uncertainties: The referent of etāṃ and trīṇi is context-dependent
items.plain_english: O beautiful-faced one, situated from the brahma knot, these are indeed the three.

items.question: What parts of the body should be permeated by the fluid in this practice?
premises: A fluid is used as the instrument
The action is to color or permeate
The permeation extends to all, beginning with the hair pores
items.inference: One should permeate everything, beginning with the hair pores, with the fluid.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should color everything, beginning with the pores of the hair, with the fluid.

items.question: Within what time period is the promised result of this practice assured?
premises: The result is affirmed to occur
There is no doubt about it
The time period is within six months
items.inference: The result certainly occurs within six months, without doubt.
items.plain_english: It indeed happens without doubt, within six months.

items.question: What sonic adornment characterizes the fluid black form in this visualization?
premises: The form is fluid and black in color
The form is adorned
The adornment consists of the sixteen vowels
items.inference: The fluid black form is adorned with the sixteen vowels.
items.plain_english: It is fluid, black in color, and adorned with the sixteen vowels.

items.question: What rejuvenating transformation occurs after six months of dedicated practice?
premises: The practice is performed for six months
The practice is repeated and sustained
Even an old person becomes youthful
items.inference: Through six months of repeated practice, even an old person becomes youthful.
uncertainties: taruṇā āyate is an unusual form; taken as becoming youthful
items.plain_english: Through six months of repeated practice, even an old person becomes youthful.

items.question: What dark form is accessed by resorting to the place of the yoginī?
premises: One resorts to the place of the yoginī
A form is encountered there
That form is dark and black-colored
items.inference: By resorting to the place of the yoginī, one accesses a dark, black-colored form.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to the place of the yoginī, one encounters a dark, black-colored form.

items.question: Which bodily region should be colored by the splendor of that dark form?
premises: The dark form possesses splendor
That splendor is used to color
The target is the region of hair, mass, and skull
items.inference: One should color the region of the hair and skull with its splendor.
uncertainties: keśa-skandha-kapāla-sthaṃ is a compact compound; parsing is interpretive
items.plain_english: One should color what is situated in the hair, shoulders, and skull with its splendor.

items.question: What ultimate freedom from aging and affliction results from this yogic practice?
premises: The practice leads to liberation from old age and death
The practitioner becomes free from disease and illness
These are stated as resulting conditions
items.inference: Through this practice one becomes freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and illness.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and illness.
